newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper names new appointee to cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper names new appointee to cenbank.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper named his third appointee to the board of directors of Colombia's central bank Thursday, a move that means a majority of the board members now owe their jobs -- if not their loyalties -- to him.

A decree said Samper had named Deputy Finance Minister Leonardo Villar, a 37-year-old economist and former deputy director of the prestigious economic think tank Fedesarrollo, to replace outgoing member Hernando Jose Gomez.
On Jan. 22, it was announced that Samper had appointed Luis Bernardo Florez, outgoing chief of the state oil company, to fill another vacancy on the bank's board.

Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo is one of seven co- directors of the bank, which operates independently of the central government and is solely responsible for setting the course of monetary policy in Colombia.

Together with another appointee named last year, this means that four of the seven board members have now been put in place by Samper, something that could conceivably tip the balance in favor of looser monetary policy as the government seeks to take the brakes off Colombia's economy.
